Naujamiestis Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Panevėžio apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Naujamiestis was founded by Karaites, brought to Lithuania from Crimea by Grand Duke Vytautas in the 15th century, who made up the majority of the town's population for roughly two centuries — until 18th-century noblemen reclaimed the lands originally granted to them, and the community faded as rabbinic Jews grew more prominent instead. By 1897, only 298 of the town's 985 residents were Jewish, with just a few Karaite families remaining. In July 1941, the town's few remaining Jews were transferred to the Panevėžys ghetto and murdered at Pajuoste forest alongside that city's own Jewish community. This cemetery is documented from the 19th century — none of its 90 surviving gravestones predate that period — and was abandoned but not demolished during the Soviet era; in 2019, surveyors discovered the original cemetery extended beyond its currently fenced boundary.
